questions.title: Which ball do you use if you find your first ball?
questions.question: You hit your first ball and think it might be lost, so you hit another ball called a provisional ball. The provisional ball lands in a great spot. But then you find your first ball on the course after looking for it. Can you choose to play the provisional ball because it's in a better spot?

choices.text: No, you have to use your first ball if you find it in time and it's not out of bounds.
Yes, you can pick whichever ball you want.
Yes, but only if everyone in your group says it's okay.
No, you always have to stop playing with the provisional ball.

questions.explanation: If you find your first ball on the course within 3 minutes, and it's in bounds, you must keep playing with your first ball, even if your provisional ball is in a better place.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A spare ball you hit if you think your first shot might be lost or out of bounds.
The ball is still on the golf course, not out of play.

questions.teachingTip: Practise using a provisional ball when playing with friends. Remind everyone which ball is the first one and which is the provisional.
likelyMisconceptions: Some players might think you can pick the ball in the best spot, but you have to play your first ball if you find it in time.

questions.title: What if the provisional ball is in a better spot?
questions.question: You hit a great shot with your provisional ball, but haven't looked for your original ball yet. If the original is found in bounds within 3 minutes, can you choose to play the provisional ball instead?

choices.text: No, you must play the original ball if found in time and in bounds.
Yes, you can choose whichever ball you like.
Yes, but only if everyone agrees.
No, the provisional ball always has to be abandoned.

questions.explanation: If you find your original ball in bounds within 3 minutes, you must play it, even if the provisional ball is in a better position.
